sector: Fuel and gas retail, home solar and power generation
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: A filling station buys fuel by the tanker load, paid in advance, and sells it at the pump for a thin margin of tens of naira per litre, so profit comes from volume and fast service, plus the shop. A gas shop buys LPG in bulk per kg and refills cylinders at a wider spread. Solar firms sell home kits for cash or in monthly instalments and earn on the hardware and finance. A power plant sells units (kWh) under a regulated tariff and only earns on the units it actually collects payment for.

caseStudies.scale: About 4.8 billion retail gallons in 2025, total fuel contribution 30.7 cents per gallon, net income $470.6 million.
caseStudies.lesson: Low-price, high-volume stations: margin per litre is tiny and swings week to week, so the game should pay for throughput and fast forecourts, with the shop as steady extra profit.

caseStudies.scale: 997,280 subscribers at end 2025; Q4 2025 subscriber value $50,165 vs creation cost $41,067 per subscriber.
caseStudies.lesson: Home solar sold on monthly payments: value is booked over many years, so cash is tight up front. Copy the gap between the cost to install and the payments collected later.

caseStudies.scale: 2025 revenue N767.6 billion, down 26%; gross margin about 10.7%; first pre-tax loss in six years, N12.5 billion.
caseStudies.lesson: Even a big branded marketer loses money when volumes fall and finance costs rise. The game should make debt and slow-moving stock expensive, and volume the main lever.

caseStudies.scale: Collected 92.2% of its bills in Q2 2026, against an average of 81.06% for all 11 distribution companies.
caseStudies.lesson: In power, billing is not cash. Metering and honest bills raise collection. The game should separate units sold from naira collected and reward prepaid meters.

costStructure.item: Fuel and gas bought from depot
costStructure.note: Most of the pump price is the product itself; TotalEnergies NG cost of sales was about 89% in 2025.
Tanker trip from depot to station, estimated N20 to N30 per litre.
Attendants, gas operator, cashier, safety officer and manager. Estimated.
Pumps run on generator diesel when grid is off; pump servicing and calibration. Estimated.
Annual licence renewals, extinguishers, leak sensors, drills, insurance. Estimated.
Land lease, loan interest on stock, pumps and tanks wear out. Estimated.
Thin: a busy, well-run station keeps about 1% to 2% of sales. Estimated.

regulation.rule: Licence to build and run a station
regulation.unitedStates: Local zoning and building permits plus state fire marshal approval under fire codes (NFPA 30A) before dispensing fuel.
regulation.nigeria: NMDPRA site suitability inspection, approval to construct, then licence to operate, with set distances from road and other stations.

regulation.unitedStates: EPA rules (40 CFR 280) require leak-proof tanks and release detection at least every 30 days, enforced with state tank programs.
regulation.nigeria: NMDPRA sets storage and tank standards under its 2025 downstream regulations; inspections at licensing and renewal.

regulation.unitedStates: State weights and measures offices test and seal pumps against NIST Handbook 44 tolerances.
regulation.nigeria: NMDPRA ordered all outlets to calibrate dispensers (Sept 2026); under-dispensing can lead to licence revocation.

regulation.unitedStates: State fire marshals and LP-gas boards enforce NFPA 58; DOT rules require cylinder requalification at set intervals.
regulation.nigeria: NMDPRA licenses and seals unlicensed LPG retailers; SON-led programme sends cylinders to authorised requalification centres (2026).

regulation.unitedStates: Market prices; many states have price-gouging laws during emergencies, enforced by state attorneys general.
regulation.nigeria: Petrol price deregulated since 2023; depots and stations set prices, NMDPRA monitors supply and quality.

regulation.unitedStates: FERC regulates wholesale power and interstate lines; state public utility commissions set retail tariffs.
regulation.nigeria: NERC sets tariff bands; Band A must get 20+ hours a day or be downgraded. Electricity Act 2023 lets states form own regulators.

gameRules.name: Prepaid tanker load
gameRules.rule: Order 1 load = 33,000 L; pay 33,000 x depotPrice (N1,350 = N44.55m) at order. Arrives next game day; 15% chance +1 day delay. Tank holds max 3 loads. Stock above 3 days of sales earns nothing extra.
gameRules.playerFeels: Order early or the pumps dry; order too much and cash sleeps in the tank.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigerian marketers pay depots before loading; working capital caps how much they sell.

gameRules.name: Pump throughput and margin
gameRules.rule: Each pump serves up to 20 cars/hour x 25 L with an attendant, 6 cars/hour without. Profit per litre = pumpPrice - landedCost. Price band is landedCost + N20 to + N80; each N10 above area price cuts arrivals 5%.
gameRules.playerFeels: Speed and queues matter more than price; greed empties the forecourt.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Retail fuel margins are cents or tens of naira per litre; volume and service drive profit.

gameRules.name: Full-litre meter test
gameRules.rule: Each pump drifts 0.1% short per game week. Inspector tests every 14 days with a 10 L can; pass if within 50 mL. Pass: Trust +10. Fail: pump sealed 1 day, fine N500,000, Trust -15. Servicing costs N50,000 and resets drift.
gameRules.playerFeels: Servicing is cheap insurance; an honest pump pulls the queue.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Weights and measures tests and NMDPRA calibration orders with licence revocation for under-dispensing.

gameRules.name: Cylinder safety check
gameRules.rule: Every cylinder needs a leak check (2 s tap) before refill. 5% of cylinders arrive expired or dented: reject and send to requalification (N5,000, back in 2 days). Skipping a check: 1 in 50 chance of leak alarm, cage shut 1 day, Trust -30.
gameRules.playerFeels: Checks take seconds; skipping them can close the shop.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NFPA 58 and Nigeria's cylinder requalification programme; retailers must refuse unsafe cylinders.

gameRules.name: Solar pay small-small
gameRules.rule: Kit price N2.4m, cost N1.8m. Deposit 30% (N720,000) then 12 x N140,000. Each month: 90% pay, 7% pay late next month, 3% default and kit locks, recovered at 50% value. Credit check (N10,000) halves default rate.
gameRules.playerFeels: More sales, slower cash; a careful loan book pays off.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Pay-as-you-go solar with remote lockout, deposits and monthly instalments (Lumos, Sunrun).

gameRules.name: Power supply hours
gameRules.rule: Plant hours/day = 24 x availability (0.75 to 0.98, +0.05 per maintenance level). Band A pays N225/kWh only on days with 20+ hours; shorter days are refunded. Cash = billed x collectionRate (80%, +3% per 10% prepaid meters, max 95%).
gameRules.playerFeels: Keeping the plant running beats selling more contracts.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NERC Band A 20-hour rule; DisCo collection 81% average, 92% best (Q2 2026).

gameRules.name: Three-paper licence ladder
gameRules.rule: Pumps locked until: site check (N2m, 3 days), approval to construct (N5m, 7 days), licence to operate (N3m, 3 days, needs Safety >= 70). Licence renews each game year for N3m; lapsed licence locks pumps.
gameRules.playerFeels: Patience and paperwork before the big money.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NMDPRA site suitability, approval to construct and operating licence steps.

gameRules.name: Serve the queue in scarcity
gameRules.rule: Scarcity event: arrivals x2 for 3 days, depot price +5%. Pump price stays in normal band. Selling all day: Trust +5/day. Closing with stock in tank: Trust -20 and inspector visit. Held stock never gains value.
gameRules.playerFeels: Shortages reward the station that keeps selling fairly.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Regulators act against hoarding and diversion during supply shortages.

stages.licenceOrGate: None; starting cash covers generator, scale and caged cylinder
Gas retail licence, fenced cage, 2 extinguishers, leak sensor, Safety >= 60
Site check then approval to construct passed; N120m for land lease and tanks
Licence to operate, first pump test passed, cash for one tanker load
Trust >= 70 and two certified solar technicians hired
Each new station passes its own licence ladder; Safety >= 75 at all branches
Depot licence, power generation licence, gas supply contract, 20 stations
Licences in each new country, 2 years with no failed safety audit

uniqueMechanics.name: Tanker order planner
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Reads tank gauges and the sales forecast, then chooses when to prepay the next 33,000 L load, balancing dry pumps against cash locked in stock.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Tank gauge panel with days-of-stock bar, depot price, cash after order and arrival time

uniqueMechanics.name: Pump test and servicing
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Watches each pump's drift, pays for servicing, and plays the inspector's 10-litre can test when it comes. Pumps can never be set to pour short.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Pump row with drift meter, service button and a can-fill animation showing exact litres

uniqueMechanics.name: Pay small-small ledger
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Approves solar buyers after a credit check, tracks monthly payments, chases late payers politely and unlocks kits when paid.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Loan book list with paid, late and locked status, cash expected this month and default rate

failureStates.trigger: Tank stock under 0.5 day of sales with no load ordered
failureStates.consequence: Drivers leave; Trust -10 per dry day
failureStates.recovery: Prepay a tanker load; arrives next day, Trust recovers +5 a day of full supply

failureStates.trigger: Two failed pump tests in 30 days or Safety score under 50
failureStates.recovery: Service all pumps, run a safety drill, pay N3m re-inspection

failureStates.trigger: Unchecked cylinder refilled (1 in 50 chance) or leak sensor not replaced for 90 days
failureStates.consequence: Cage closed 1 day, Trust -30, safety officer report
failureStates.recovery: Replace sensor (N150,000), retrain operator, pass next safety check

failureStates.trigger: Solar defaults above 10% or cash below the cost of the next container
failureStates.recovery: Turn on credit checks, collect late payments, sell kits for cash only for a month

failureStates.trigger: Supply under 20 hours on 3 days in a week
failureStates.consequence: Band A days refunded; bulk contract buyers may leave (20% chance each)
failureStates.recovery: Raise maintenance level, secure gas supply, rebuild 20-hour streak for 14 days

balanceNotes: Payback: kiosk about 1.5 months, gas shop 2, station 12 (land, tanks and first load), solar bay 3, each branch about 10, depot and plant about 35, group stage long-term. Players will feel stuck at stage 3 (N120m with only gas income) and stage 7 (N60bn); offer a bank loan or partner equity there. Tune first: petrol margin (N20 to N80), tanker delay odds and solar default rate. Keep the margin cap so hoarding never pays.
openQuestions: Should petrol margin follow live-like weekly swings (as in real deregulated pricing) or stay fixed so new players can plan?
Should the depot and power plant be financed with a loan or partner equity, and who controls the plant if a partner owns part?
Solar kits: allow an optional interest charge on instalments, or keep pay small-small interest-free for simplicity?
After the Electricity Act 2023, should state power regulators be a separate licence step or stay merged into one national regulator?
